instructions: Peel and devein the 1.25 lbs shrimp if they aren't already. Pat them dry and toss them with 1/4 tsp of the salt and the 1/4 tsp black pepper.
Finely chop the shallot and the 3 garlic cloves. Halve the pint of cherry tomatoes and halve 1/3 cup of the olives. Cut the 6 oz feta into small cubes. Finely chop 1/4 cup of the dill.
Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium. Add the shallot and cook it for 2 minutes, until it softens. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and the last 1/4 tsp salt. Turn the heat up to medium high and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until most of the tomatoes have burst and gone jammy.
Stir in the olives and 3/4 cup water. Turn the heat down to medium low and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until it's saucy and slightly thickened.

Tuck the shrimp into the sauce in a single layer. Cover the pan and cook for about 3 minutes, until the shrimp are pink and curled into a loose C. Don't let them go longer. Tightly curled shrimp are tough.
Take the pan off the heat. Grate the zest of the lemon over the top and squeeze in its juice. Stir in the dill.
Scatter the feta over the shrimp and drizzle with the last 1 tbsp olive oil. Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: All three cook a quick tomato sauce, add the shrimp only for the last few minutes and finish with feta and fresh herbs. Skinnytaste bursts cherry tomatoes with shallot, garlic and olives and finishes with lemon and dill; My Greek Dish sears the shrimp separately, flames them with ouzo and melts the feta under a lid; Supergolden Bakes simmers a passata and wine sauce for 20 to 30 minutes and browns the feta under the broiler. This one follows Skinnytaste's 30-minute method and ratios.
